title: HTAN Multiplex IHC Image Cytometry V0.1
author: Shamilene Sivagnanam
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bsqjndun
materials: DOWNLOAD SOFTWARE AND CODE Download or clone the MultiplexIHC_Code.zip file that contains all the functions and code for image processing. Save and unzip this folder somewhere other than your Downloads directory. git@github.com:Sivoyer/MultiplexIHC_Code.git Multiplex IHC Code ├── AEC_CMYK_ColorDecon.ijm ├── CP_DiscoveryPanelTemplate.cpproj ├── CommandLine │ ├── AEC_CMYK_ColorDecon.txt │ ├── CL_Registration │ │ ├── get_image_sets.m │ │ ├── parse_xml.m │ │ ├── register_SURF.m │ │ ├── run_mIHC_registration.m │ │ └── sort_regions.m │ └── Nuclei_BinaryMask.txt ├── Nuclei_BinaryMask.ijm ├── README.md └── Registration ├── get_image_sets.m ├── mIHC_Registration.m ├── parse_xml.m ├── register_SURF.m └── sort_regions.m In addition to this code, you will also need the following software installed: Registration is performed in Matlab R2018b or higher: MatLab R2018b Additional toolboxes required: Computer Vision Toolbox Color Deconvolution and Nuclei Segmentation is performed in FIJI: FIJI (FIJI Is Just ImageJ) Additional files required: RGB_to_CMYK.class To install this .class file, drag and drop into FIJI bar, then close and restart the program. Single Cell Quantification is performed in Cell Profiler 3: Cell Profiler
Select the rectangle tool for annotating boxes.
Pipeline Run Options This can be run using the software interfaces (code free), or by terminal. Instructions for both methods are listed below:

steps.title: Define naming conventions
steps.instruction: Use a consistent folder and file naming scheme: each slide folder name consists of one letter followed by six digits (e.g., H342253). Each image file name follows the pattern Initials_StudyID_UniqueSlideID_PanelName_CycleRound_Marker.SVS, such as GG_HTAN1_H342253_D18_C01R1_PD1.svs or GG_HTAN1_H342253_D18_C01R2_PDL1.svs. Apply this convention to all images saved during acquisition.

steps.title: Create folder hierarchy
steps.instruction: Create a parent study folder (e.g., HTAN1) that contains a subfolder for each slide (e.g., H342253). Inside each slide folder place all marker SVS files and exactly three hematoxylin images: an initial HEM (C00R1), a second HEM after antigen retrieval (C01R3), and a final HEM at the end of the panel (C11R3). Do not duplicate scans. Follow the example tree shown in the protocol.

steps.title: Annotate regions of interest
steps.instruction: In Aperio ImageScope (Windows only), open the last‑cycle hematoxylin SVS for the slide, select the rectangle tool, and draw square or rectangular boxes covering tissue of good quality (no folds, loss, or deformation). Each box should contain ≤ ≈65 000 cells (the downstream ROI cell‑classification limit). Save the annotations; ImageScope writes an XML file with the same base name as the image. Keep the XML in the slide folder and do not rename or move it.

substeps.instruction: 1. Open the final hematoxylin image (e.g., GG_HTAN1_H342253_D18_C11R3_HEM.svs) in ImageScope.
3. Draw uniformly sized square/rectangle boxes on high‑quality tissue; ensure each box ≤ ≈65 000 cells.
4. View the list of annotations via Annotations → Detailed View.
5. Close the SVS file, answer “yes” to save annotations, and leave the XML file in the slide folder.

steps.title: Register marker images (MATLAB)
steps.instruction: Run the MultiplexIHC registration script to align every marker image to the final‑cycle hematoxylin image. The script detects keypoints (preferring the blue channel, falling back to other RGB channels if needed), computes a similarity‑based geometric transform, applies it to all channels, and saves the registered RGB as a TIFF in an automatically created Registered_Regions/ROIxx folder for each slide.

substeps.instruction: 1. Open MATLAB and click the “choose folder” icon to set the working path to the MultiplexIHC_Code directory.
2. In the Current Folder panel, right‑click the MultiplexIHC_Code folder and select Add to Path → Selected Folders and Subfolders (folders turn black).
3. Double‑click mIHC_Registration.m to open it in the editor.
4. In the Editor tab, click Run to start the script.
5. When prompted, select the Parent folder that contains all slide folders.
1. Use the MATLAB executable (e.g., /Applications/MATLAB_R2018b.app/bin/matlab) with flags -nodesktop -nosplash.

2. Execute: "cd('<CODE_DIR>');run_mIHC_registration('<PARENT_DIR>');exit;" where <CODE_DIR> is the path to the MultiplexIHC_RegistrationCode directory and <PARENT_DIR> is the path to the study’s parent folder.

steps.title: Check registration quality
steps.instruction: After registration, inspect the Parent/Registration_Check folder, which contains low‑resolution preview images prefixed with regck_ for each ROI. Verify proper alignment; if an ROI is mis‑registered, either exclude it from downstream analysis or locate the Redo_ROI folder inside the slide, which holds the failed marker and hematoxylin images for manual re‑registration.

steps.title: Run AEC color deconvolution (FIJI CLI)
steps.instruction: Execute the FIJI macro that extracts the AEC signal via RGB‑to‑CMYK conversion with maximum gray component replacement, adds the Y and M channels, caps pixel values at 255, and rescales the middle 90 % to 0‑255. Run the command: java -jar /Applications/Fiji.app/jars/ij-1.52p.jar -ijpath /Applications/Fiji.app -batch <CODE_DIR>/AEC_CMYK_ColorDecon.txt <PARENT_DIR>. The script creates a Processed folder inside each slide, mirroring the Registered_Regions structure, and prefixes each output image with V_.

steps.title: Run AEC deconvolution (FIJI GUI)
steps.instruction: Open FIJI, choose Plugins → Macros → Run…, select the AEC_ColorDeconCMYK.ijm file from the MultiplexIHC_Code directory, then select the Parent study folder. The macro creates the same Processed/ROIxx folders and V_‑prefixed images as the command‑line version.

steps.title: Segment nuclei on final hematoxylin
steps.instruction: Use the Nuclei_BinaryMask FIJI macro to generate binary masks of nuclei from the last‑cycle hematoxylin image. The macro performs color deconvolution with the H + AEC vector, background subtraction, Otsu thresholding, point‑maxima detection (using a user‑specified noise tolerance), EDM watershed, and erosion‑dilation steps. Run: Plugins → Macros → Run…, select Nuclei_BinaryMask.ijm, choose the Parent folder, and at the Noise parameter prompt enter the expected noise tolerance (or accept the default). Output masks are saved alongside the processed images.

steps.title: Measure single‑cell features (CellProfiler)
steps.instruction: Launch CellProfiler with the provided template project (CellProfiler_TemplateInstructions.pdf) located in the MultiplexIHC_Code directory. Load the V_ images from the Processed/ROIxx folders, configure modules to measure mean intensity for each marker, object area, object index, and centroid X/Y coordinates. Export the results in the format required by FCS Express Image Cytometry for downstream single‑cell classification.

steps.title: Convert to OME‑TIFF
steps.instruction: For each ROI, combine the set of V_ images into a single OME‑TIFF file using Bio‑Formats (e.g., bfconvert). The resulting OME‑TIFFs can be used for downstream analysis and archiving.
